flow_lines.method: D8 steepest descent on a 3x3-smoothed, pit-filled (priority-flood) grid; kept only if the line reaches the mapped channel (within 1 cell), drops at least 15 m, is at least 2.5 km long, and never climbs or needs filling by more than 3 m on the unfilled grid

flood.label: Illustrative flood spread
flood.image_values: red*256+green: 0..60000 = share of the spread on that bank when the cell is reached (0 first); 65535 = never; blue/40 = bank index

elevation.source: Terrain Tiles (Mapzen/Tilezen terrarium, AWS Open Data), zoom 12; SRTM here (U.S. Geological Survey)

river_level.rule: lowest channel cell within 1 cell of the mapped line, rolling median over about 2 km, then made non-increasing downstream

flood.method: Fill and spill on about 35 m cells from one entry per river bank: the next cell is always the lowest one next to the water reached so far (8 neighbours), so a hollow fills before water spills over its lowest rim. Water never crosses the mapped river line (3 cells wide). The entry on each bank is, by rule, the bank cell inside the study area that is lowest relative to the river level beside it. The study-area frame is not a barrier. Each bank's spread is drawn up to the point where the data stops supporting a direction.
flood.support_rule: The fill is repeated 12 times with correlated noise added to the elevation (sd 1.0 m, patches of about 240 m; seed 57). For growing areas, the overlap (intersection over union, on 6 x 6 cell blocks of about 210 m) between each run and the plain run is measured. The runs must agree (mean overlap >= 0.6) somewhere within the first 1.0 km2; the front is then drawn until the mean overlap falls below 0.6 at two steps in a row. After that the direction depends on errors in the elevation itself, and the scene says the path is uncertain. If the runs never agree early, only the first 0.1 km2 is drawn.
flood.not_supported: Whether or where water really left the channel; embankment, road and canal heights below the 35 m grid; culverts, drains, depth, speed, timing and volume. Shapes are schematic, not reliable at street or house scale.

Their heights are not in the data, so they are not added as walls or channels: whatever the elevation grid already shows of them is in the fill, nothing more.
